```json
{
  "answer": "15.52% of reviews from electronics products priced at most $40 with review bodies longer than 500 characters are 1-star (214 of 1,379 reviews).",
  "sql": "WITH elec AS (SELECT ref_id, prc AS price_usd FROM items_g1 WHERE main_cat = 'All Electronics' UNION ALL SELECT ref_id, prc_usd AS price_usd FROM items_g2 WHERE main_cat = 'All Electronics' UNION ALL SELECT ref_id, prc AS price_usd FROM items_g3 WHERE main_cat = 'All Electronics'), eligible AS (SELECT ref_id FROM elec WHERE price_usd IS NOT NULL AND price_usd <= 40), revs AS (SELECT f.rtg FROM fdbk_g1 f JOIN eligible e ON f.ref_id = e.ref_id WHERE LENGTH(f.body) > 500 UNION ALL SELECT f.rtg FROM fdbk_g2 f JOIN eligible e ON f.ref_id = e.ref_id WHERE LENGTH(f.body) > 500 UNION ALL SELECT f.rtg FROM fdbk_g3 f JOIN eligible e ON f.ref_id = e.ref_id WHERE LENGTH(f.body) > 500) SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN rtg = 1.0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_1star FROM revs"
}
```

Notes on assumptions verified along the way:
- The catalog is split across three parallel table groups (`items_g1/g2/g3` + `fdbk_g1/g2/g3`), so the query unions all three; since no group was specified, the result covers the whole database.
- Price units were checked: `items_g2.prc` is in cents (max 2,688,800), so `prc_usd` was used for that group; `items_g1.prc` and `items_g3.prc` are already in USD.
- "Electronics" was interpreted as `main_cat = 'All Electronics'` (the dominant electronics category; "Car Electronics" was excluded — flagged as an interpretation in the memory notes).
- Exact duplicate review rows exist in the feedback tables, but in this slice they were only 17 of 1,379 rows, so row-level counting was used (dedup would not materially change the result).
